description.p: Skribisto is a writing app for novels, from the first idea to the finished manuscript.
Skribisto est un logiciel d'écriture pour les romans, de la première idée au manuscrit terminé.

ul.li: Split panes and tabs, and a whole chapter, part or book readable as one text
Écran partagé et onglets, et un chapitre, une partie ou le livre entier à lire comme un seul texte
Corkboard, story bible, margin comments and footnotes
Tableau de liège, bible narrative, commentaires dans la marge et notes de bas de page
Word goals, writing sessions, pace planning and manuscript analysis
Objectifs de mots, sessions d'écriture, planification du rythme et analyse du manuscrit
Statuses you name yourself, from first draft to final
Des statuts que vous nommez vous-même, du premier jet à la version finale
Import from Scrivener, Manuskript, Plume Creator, Word, OpenDocument or Markdown, comments included, with a report of anything left behind
Import depuis Scrivener, Manuskript, Plume Creator, Word, OpenDocument ou Markdown, commentaires compris, avec un rapport de ce qui n'a pas pu être repris
Export to DOCX, ODT, EPUB, PDF and more, and finish the page layout in the program you prefer
Export en DOCX, ODT, EPUB, PDF et d'autres formats, pour finir la mise en page dans le logiciel de votre choix
Search and replace, autosave, backups and version history
Rechercher et remplacer, enregistrement automatique, sauvegardes et historique des versions
Spell checking, smart punctuation and 24 interface languages
Correcteur orthographique, ponctuation intelligente et interface en 24 langues
Built for accessibility: screen readers, braille displays and keyboard shortcuts
Pensé pour l'accessibilité : lecteurs d'écran, plages braille et raccourcis clavier

screenshot.caption: The binder and the editor, with prose and its synopsis side by side
Le classeur et l'éditeur, avec le texte et son synopsis côte à côte
The launcher, listing recent projects and bundled examples
Le lanceur, avec les projets récents et les exemples fournis

ul.li: Resources: attach files and web links to any item of your project, a map of the village, a photograph, the recording of an interview, a page on the web. They are listed in a new panel on the right, Resources (Ctrl+Shift+X), which shows those of the item you are on. Add files with its + button or by dropping them from your file manager, and web links with its globe button, by dropping an address from your browser, or with Ctrl+V. Each row shows the file's type, a preview for a picture, its size or its address, and says Not found when a linked file is not where it was
A file larger than 10 MB asks before it is added: store it in the project, where it travels with every copy and every backup, or link to it where it is. Don't ask again keeps your answer
Settings ▸ Editor ▸ Editor Behavior has a new choice for those files: Ask each time, Always store in the project or Always link to the file. Reset to defaults brings the question back

Double-click a resource to open it in the application your system uses for that kind of file, a picture in the image viewer and a web link in your browser. A file that could start a program, such as a script or an installer, asks first and offers Show in folder instead, since a project can come from someone else

Change a stored file in another application, a map you annotate or a recording you trim, and Skribisto takes the new version into the project when you come back to its window, before each save, and when you close the project. In a project kept as a single file, a notice says so and offers Undo. Such a project opens its files as copies, which are removed when it closes

Drag a resource into a text to link to it there. A picture asks whether to put the picture itself in the text or a link to it. Ctrl+click on such a link opens the resource, and an export prints only the link's words

A file that is not a picture, dropped on a text, becomes a resource of that item, linked where you dropped it. The notice that says so offers Undo, which takes back both the resource and the link, or neither when you have typed before the link since, and says so

Drag a resource onto an item in the binder to attach it to that item too, or choose Attach to items… in its menu to pick several items in the binder. A resource dropped in a text is attached to that text's item

In a resource's menu, Locate… finds a linked file that moved, and links again any other missing file from the same folder found in the new one. Rename and describe… gives a resource a title and a description of its own. Detach from this item takes it off the item, and Remove from the project takes it out of every item
Removing a resource from the project, or detaching it from an item, shows a message with Undo, which brings it back as it was

Every folder has a new view, Resources: the files and web links attached to the folder and to everything inside it, each listed once with the items it is on, as a list or as a grid of tiles. Click an item's name to open it. Files and links added there, or dropped on it, are attached to the folder. A plain folder, which showed only its synopsis, now has a bar with two views, Folder and Resources

Settings ▸ Work has a new page, Resources, for the files and links attached to no item any more: attach them to items chosen in the binder, export copies of them to a folder, or remove them from the project. It also says how much room the project's stored files take, and offers a single-file project past 100 MB to be saved as a folder, which saves faster
A project kept as a single file whose stored files pass 100 MB offers, once, to be saved as a folder instead, which saves only what changed

The Gallery shows the picture resources of its notes too, after the pictures in their text, marked Resource, and those of the folder itself first. They open in the image viewer with the others, and a right click offers the Resources panel's menu. A search in the Gallery also finds a picture resource by its title, file name or description

Global search has a new switch, Resources, on by default: it finds resources by their titles, descriptions, file names and web addresses, under each item they are attached to. A replace never changes them
The Help window has a new page, Files and links for your research

Importing a Scrivener project now brings the files of your research inside the new project: pictures, PDF files, sounds and web pages become resources of the folder they sat in, or of their own note when they had a synopsis, notes or keywords. A plain text file still becomes a note holding its words. In your manuscript, a picture stays a note showing it, and any other file becomes a resource of its note. Nothing is copied beside the new project any more, so that choice is gone from the Save page

Before a Scrivener import, the review page says how many research files the new project will hold and how much room they take. A file that cannot be read, or is larger than 512 MB, stays in your Scrivener project, and the import's report names it

Scrivener bookmarks to web pages and to files on your computer come across as link resources of the document that held them, and the project's own as resources of the project. They used to be lines in the notes of the From Scrivener folder

A picture wider than its text is drawn at the width of the text, its height in proportion, in every text. It used to keep its own size and run past the right edge, which is how screenshots imported from Scrivener often looked. Nothing in the project changes: widen the window, or the column, and the picture grows back up to its own size. Resize the image now works from the size you see: 50 halves it

Double-click a picture, or choose View the image in its menu, to open it in the new image viewer: as large as the window allows, with Zoom in, Zoom out, Fit and 100 %, Ctrl and the mouse wheel to zoom where you point, a pinch on a trackpad, and a drag to move around a large picture. The arrow keys go to the text's previous and next pictures. Save a copy… writes the picture to a file under its original name, and Open in another app opens it in your system's picture application
On a Book's page, View beside the cover, or a double click on it, opens the cover in the image viewer

A notes folder has a new view, Gallery: the pictures of its notes as thumbnails in columns, each keeping its proportions. First image shows one per note with the number of its other pictures, All images shows every one. Nested shows each subfolder as a tile with its first four pictures, Flat shows the pictures of every subfolder at once, and Notes without images adds the text notes as tiles of their opening words. The Image size slider makes the thumbnails smaller or larger

The Gallery and the Overview share their search, their tag and status filters and their order. A double click on a thumbnail opens the image viewer over the pictures the Gallery shows, in its order; a right click offers Open the note
The Help window has a new page, Pictures and the gallery
In global search, choose Open in editor from a result's menu, or middle-click the result, to open it in the active editor pane, scrolled to the match with the matching text selected

A note that is a story bible entry, because it carries a tag with Find in prose turned on, shows a solid note icon instead of the outlined one: in the binder, the editor tabs, the corkboard, the Overview, the Trash, Go to, the destination pickers and Export. Turning Find in prose on or off for a tag changes the icon of every note carrying it at once, and a screen reader announces such a row as a story bible entry

A notes folder has an icon of its own, a folder holding a solid note, instead of the note icon it shared with the notes inside it: in the binder, the editor tabs, the Overview, the Trash, Go to, the destination pickers, Export, the Create menus and Convert to

A click in the empty page around a text now puts the cursor in it: in the margin beside a line, at the start or the end of that line; under the text, at its end. A tap with a finger does the same. With a short text, a click on the empty part of the page used to do nothing

With the editor split in two, a click anywhere in a half, even on its margin or under its cards, makes it the active half, and the panels on the right show its item. A click used to count only when it put the cursor in a field. The cursor stays where it was

In the New Work window, the Tags, Workflow and Note templates choices have a page of their own, Organization, after Template, where they no longer sit below the fold. Each now says what it creates, right under its list: the tags of the chosen palette, the stages of the chosen workflow and the templates of the chosen set

In the New Work window, No tags, No templates and No structure are now in their lists, so a choice made there can be taken back. Once a palette, a set of templates or a book structure had been picked, there was no way back to none but to cancel the window

A spelling dictionary found on your computer but not offered for download, such as Esperanto in /usr/share/hunspell, can now be chosen as the language of a project or a scene. It used to appear under Settings ▸ Dictionaries ▸ Installed, sometimes marked unusable, and was missing from the list of languages. It is listed by its own name and code, Esperanto (eo), so English (en-ZA) and English (en-IE) can be told apart

Opening and saving a project with many pictures takes far less memory. Every save used to read all of the project's pictures into memory, and a single-file project was unpacked into the system's temporary folder, which on many Linux systems is memory too. Pictures are now copied straight from file to file, and a single-file project is unpacked into Skribisto's own data folder on disk
A project kept as a folder and saved as a single file with Save As keeps its pictures. The first save of the new file used to look for them in the wrong place and leave every one of them out

A project kept as a folder is never read or saved through a symbolic link any more. A scene, a list of the project or a footnote file that is a link to a file elsewhere stops the project from opening, and the message names it; a linked picture, stored file, comment or history entry is left out with a warning. Before, the file the link pointed at was read in, and a copy or a backup of the project carried it along

On the corkboard, the tooltips of Nested and Flat say what each one shows, and Settings ▸ Corkboard says that Flat shows everything in the container, folder cards included, in reading order. They only said that the choice applies to every corkboard, and that Flat showed every scene

The About page of the Launcher now shows what Help ▸ About shows, and both show more: links to the source code, Discord and the place to report a problem, the libraries and fonts Skribisto is built with, and the full text of each licence, all readable without a connection. The Launcher's page used to hold a single line

In About, What's new in this version opens this version's release notes, in English, and Copy version info puts the version, the system and how Skribisto was installed on the clipboard, ready to paste into a bug report
